landing.title: Automated femoral & tibial torsion
landing.subtitle: Upload a lower-limb MRI examination and get segmentation, torsion angles, and editable measurement landmarks — computed automatically and reviewable in the browser.
landing.disclaimer: Research tool — not intended for clinical use.

howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.intro: From a raw DICOM export to reviewed torsion angles in a few steps.

upload.title: Upload
upload.body: Select the whole examination folder. The DICOM series are enumerated and previewed — no manual sorting.

select.title: Select series
select.body: Pick the whole-leg series (auto-split into hip, knee and ankle) or assign three separate region series.

compute.title: Compute
compute.body: A GPU pipeline segments the bones and computes femoral and tibial torsion — queued and run in the background.

review.title: Review
review.body: Inspect the volume, drag the measurement landmarks, and watch the angles update live before saving.

femoral.title: Femoral torsion
femoral.body: Both the Lee and Murphy landmark methods, per side, so you can compare definitions on the same scan.

tibial.title: Tibial torsion
tibial.body: Proximal and distal reference axes measured on their native slices, with the signed angle shown per line.

interactive.title: Interactive review
interactive.body: Reference-line landmarks are draggable — including across slices — and every edit is saved back to the examination.

cta.title: Ready to start?
cta.body: Upload an examination to run the pipeline, or read more about the measurements and how they are computed.

about.title: About
about.intro: A web front end for computing and reviewing lower-limb torsion measurements from MRI, built on the open-source morphometry analysis library.

measures.title: What it measures
measures.intro: The tool derives rotational alignment of the lower limb from a segmentation of the femur, tibia and fibula:
measures.femoral: Femoral torsion — the angle between the femoral neck axis and the posterior condylar axis, computed with both the Lee and Murphy landmark definitions for each side.
measures.tibial: Tibial torsion — the angle between the proximal tibial axis and the trans-malleolar axis at the ankle, per side.
measures.note: Each measurement is defined by a pair of reference lines on their native acquisition slices. Because both bones are highly anisotropic in these scans (fine in-plane, coarse through-plane), the viewer renders native axial slices rather than a resliced volume, and the landmarks are placed on the slice they were measured on.

pipeline.title: The pipeline
pipeline.intro: An upload is turned into reviewable measurements by a sequence of background steps:

ingestion.title: Ingestion
ingestion.body: The uploaded examination folder is scanned for DICOM series, which are grouped, cleaned of non-image files, and previewed so the correct series can be chosen.

segmentation.title: Segmentation
segmentation.body: A deep-learning model (nnU-Net) segments the hip, knee and ankle regions into bone labels on a GPU. Jobs are serialised through a single worker so the GPU is never oversubscribed.

torsion.title: Torsion computation
torsion.body: The morphometry library derives the anatomical landmarks and reference axes from the segmentation masks and computes the femoral and tibial torsion angles.

review.title: Review & correction
review.body: Results are presented in the interactive viewer. Landmarks can be dragged — within a slice or across slices — and the angles recompute live; corrections are saved back to the examination.

analysis.title: Analysis & API
analysis.body: A Python morphometry library computes the measurements from segmentation masks. A FastAPI service handles DICOM ingestion, stores examinations, and dispatches segmentation and torsion jobs to a Redis-backed worker running containerised models.

web.title: Web interface
web.body: This front end is a Next.js / React application. The examination viewer renders the NIfTI volumes directly in the browser with Cornerstone3D and draws the draggable measurement landmarks on top.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.body: This is a research and development tool. It is not a medical device and is not intended for clinical use, diagnosis, or treatment decisions. Automated measurements can be wrong and must always be verified by a qualified reader.
